history.dynasty: Local accounts: 18th century; unverified claims of Maratha patronage and (per one AI-generated site) commissioning by Maratha Sardar Bhaskar Rao Pandit
history.period: Claimed ~250 years old (18th century); one tourism blog asserts a Pandava-era legend — conflict noted in summary
history.summary: Devi Mandir on Devi Mandir Road, Tehsil Camp, Panipat, is dedicated to Goddess Durga and is a major city shrine. Popular local accounts (testbook Q&A summaries) put its age at about 250 years (18th century) and note it stands by a former drought pond, now converted into a park used for morning/evening walks; an annual Ramlila has been staged in the park during Navratri for roughly 100 years. CONFLICT: a tourism blog (Wanderon) instead claims the Pandavas founded it in the Mahabharata era, with the idol found buried by a local farmer — treat as legend, not fact. An AI-generated heritage site (inheritage.foundation) additionally claims Maratha Sardar Bhaskar Rao Pandit commissioned it and that it is ASI-protected; neither claim is corroborated by any other source and should be treated as unverified. No inscription or archaeological record found; the 18th-century date is the only widely repeated figure.

name: Shri Devi Mandir, Panipat
town_description: Panipat, on the GT Road about 90 km north of Delhi, is famous as the site of three decisive battles (1526, 1556, 1761) and is today a major textile and handloom hub. It became a separate district from Karnal on 31 October 1989.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (~110 km)
travel.road: Devi Mandir Road, Tehsil Camp, Panipat 132103 — on/near GT Road (NH-44)

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; Navratri for the main festival season
